summary: The Definition Unit Tests (DUT, Condition C) method is effective. On both Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Condition C significantly outperforms the engagement-matched neutral-checks baseline (Condition B) in overall accuracy and across all 3 convention families. The primary decision criterion is fully met on both models. The method should proceed to further analysis.
analysis: Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct: C achieves 95.0% overall accuracy vs B at 90.0% (+5.0pp, bootstrap 95% CI [+2.0%, +8.3%], excludes 0). C > B in all 3 families: asymptotics +2pp, completeness +12pp, convolution +1pp. Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct: C achieves 81.3% overall accuracy vs B at 58.7% (+22.7pp, bootstrap 95% CI [+16.0%, +29.3%], excludes 0). C > B in all 3 families: asymptotics +4pp, completeness +61pp, convolution +3pp. The engagement-matched control (B) effectively rules out the extra-computation confound since B performs comparably to A on both models. DUT also massively outperforms 5-sample majority vote (A@5, B@5) on both models, demonstrating a qualitatively different benefit from inference-time scaling. Condition C reduces alternate-convention match rates by ~80% relative to B on both models.
reason: The primary decision rule is fully satisfied: (1) C improves over B by >= 5pp on both models (Qwen: +5.0pp, Llama: +22.7pp), with paired bootstrap 95% CIs excluding zero. (2) C > B holds in 3 of 3 convention families on both models, exceeding the 2/3 requirement. The discriminative definition checks in DUT provide a genuine accuracy benefit beyond engagement-matched neutral checks, and the effect generalizes across model strengths (high-baseline Qwen vs low-baseline Llama) and all convention types. Verdict is 'good' -- proceed with further experiments.
